title: Duskmourn: House of Horror Promos: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "Don't be a wimp. We'll cover more ground this way." —Rian, former survivor
"Sure, I'm pretty small, but Gribble isn't, so I don't get scared."
"The readings are off the charts! Whatever it is, it's close."
It slices away the most precious memories first, then the mundane, until all that remains is blank, formless fear.
"See?! That's why you always burn the bodies." —Rip, spawn hunter
Valgavoth whispered into Marina's ear until he was all she could hear.
"All stars grow dark. All worlds come to an end."
Vicky was so tired. The pain began to fade. "You were so brave," said her grandmother's voice from somewhere far away. "But it's time to rest now."
Cracks in the facade of the House lead not to escape but to oblivion.
"Stitch your eyes, stitch your skin, stitch your mouth into a grin."
She sees the faces of those who wronged her in everyone she encounters.
The melody was all in her head, but she'd always preferred to dance alone.
She's got a heart of gold, a nose for danger, and jaws that can pulverize a cellarspawn with a single snap.
Life thrives in the Hauntwoods, but it follows its own laws, unbound from the natural order.
"They just keep coming and coming—perfect for my morning workout!"
Tyvar and the Wanderer were done running.
Those who glimpse the House's true nature firsthand are cursed to never again look away.
Farley had always been the fastest on the track team. But no one was cheering anymore.
In a moment of bloodthirsty whimsy, a razorkin once picked up a ventriloquist's puppet and used it to terrorize a survivor. Now it hunts on its own, with no one pulling its strings.
Here, the Balemurk spits and boils, the oppressive darkness pierced by scorching spears of fire.
Here, the Mistmoors slump like a grieving parent, the once-thriving fields drowned by the relentless deluge.
Here, the Floodpits languish like a corpse, the clear waters choked by the filthy hands of the bog.
Here, the Hauntwoods churn like a viper's nest, as monstrous creatures prowl hungrily toward the ghostly light.
Here, the Boilerbilges twitch like a trapped animal, peaks straining against the grasping roots and vines.
It is the one chamber whose location never changes, the rotten, rancorous heart of Duskmourn itself.
